rootCause: The eraser's target-selection policy is "every object whose geometry the swept eraser disk touches, on the whole page" — there is no z-order ranking, no topmost-first resolution, and no ink-only restriction on the destructive lane. Concretely: (1) the commit engine erasePageAnnotations iterates ALL page objects and applies the erase to every one the stroke intersects — path objects at pageSpaceEraser.js:1089-1107 and ALL non-path objects (shapes, text, stamps, images) at pageSpaceEraser.js:1140-1147, where any touch = whole delete; (2) the policy function getEraserOperation (eraserPolicy.js:66-69) PROMOTES every non-ink object to 'entire' (whole-delete) even when the user is in partial/pixel-erase mode, so erasing a bit of ink that overlaps a rectangle also whole-deletes the rectangle; (3) the per-object hit test eraserStrokeTouchesObject (eraserHitTest.js:88-95) returns an independent boolean per object with no ordering, and filled objects hit-test their ENTIRE interior (geometryHitTest.js:903-909 for rects), so a stack of filled shapes under one eraser pass all report hits; (4) the live preview lanes classifyEraserSegment (FabricEraserCanvas.jsx:1669-1689) and ghostAtomicHits (FabricEraserCanvas.jsx:1596-1620) use the same all-hits enumeration, and the parallel callout and survey-marker lanes (FabricEraserCanvas.jsx:1852-1853, surveyMarkerEraser.js:44-70) likewise collect every intersecting hit. The only filters ever applied are permission/lock/scope gates (getEraseBlockReason, FabricEraserCanvas.jsx:1522-1586; canModify re-check at PDFViewer.jsx:27100-27115) — none of them consider stacking. Meanwhile z-order IS well-defined and available: SVGAnnotationLayer paints objects[] in array-index order (SVGAnnotationLayer.jsx:2045 for-loop; SVG paint order = document order), so higher index = topmost — the eraser simply never consults it. The result set then commits atomically to the Yjs doc via buildEraseIntent → handleEraseIntent → commitDurableEraseIntent (FabricEraserCanvas.jsx:1975-1997, PDFViewer.jsx:27063-27139), faithfully persisting the over-broad deletion.

professionalBehavior: All four reference apps restrict the eraser to ink (pen/highlighter) strokes and never destroy other annotation types under the path, let alone a whole stack. Bluebeam Revu: the Eraser tool removes only Pen and free-form (pen-mode) Highlighter markups; small/medium/large heads pixel-erase those strokes, and the separate 'Annotation Eraser' removes parts of a single pen/highlighter action — rectangles, clouds, text, stamps, etc. are untouched and must be selected+deleted (support.bluebeam.com Revu Eraser-Tool help). Adobe Acrobat: the 'Erase drawing' tool erases only free-form Draw/Pencil-tool markups; it cannot touch shapes, text boxes, stamps, or page content (Adobe help + community.adobe.com threads). GoodNotes: the eraser works only on pen & highlighter strokes — never typed text, images, PDF content, or inserted elements; its 'erase entire stroke' option deletes whole strokes on touch and there is an 'erase only highlighter' filter, i.e. type-filtered erasing is a first-class concept (support.goodnotes.com 'Erase content' and 'Erasing handwriting and highlighting'). PDF Expert: the eraser lives in the drawing toolset and applies to pencil/drawing strokes (pdfexpert.com 'How to draw on PDFs'); its docs are less explicit than the others, so I state this with slight hedging, but no documentation suggests it deletes non-ink annotation types. Net industry norm: an eraser pass may carve MULTIPLE overlapping INK strokes (that part of Survey's behavior is standard), but non-ink objects are simply not erasable by the eraser; the 'delete a whole object by touching it' operation is a separate explicit mode, and no app whole-deletes every object type stacked under the path. Sources: https://support.bluebeam.com/online-help/revu21/Content/RevuHelp/Menus/Tools/Markup/Eraser-Tool--V.htm , https://community.adobe.com/t5/acrobat/how-can-i-erase-pencil-pen-marks-on-a-pdf-using-acrobat-11/m-p/4769200 , https://support.goodnotes.com/hc/en-us/articles/7353718249231-Erase-content , https://support.goodnotes.com/hc/en-us/articles/4402912570895-Erasing-handwriting-and-highlighting , https://pdfexpert.com/how-to-draw-on-pdf
proposedFix: Two-part minimal design, all in page-unit target-selection logic (no touch to canvas sizing, zoomGeneration, or SVG viewBox scaling). PART 1 — ink-only partial mode (matches all four reference apps): add a third operation 'skip' to getEraserOperation (src/utils/eraserPolicy.js:66-69): when requestedMode==='partial' and the annotation is not partial-eligible, return 'skip' instead of 'entire'. In erasePageAnnotations, skip-operation path objects are left untouched (don't push into pathGroups.full at pageSpaceEraser.js:1093-1105) and the non-path whole-delete loop (pageSpaceEraser.js:1140-1147) runs only when mode==='full'/'entire'. Mirror the same policy in the preview lanes so preview can never disagree with commit (the codebase's own stated invariant, FabricEraserCanvas.jsx:1594-1595): classifyEraserSegment (1681-1682) stops collecting atomicIds in partial mode, ghostAtomicHits (1604) early-returns in partial mode, and the callout (1852) and survey-marker (1853) delete lanes become entire-mode-only. PART 2 — topmost-only in entire (object-eraser) mode: inside erasePageAnnotations, after computing raw hits but before building deletedIndexes, resolve per eraser SAMPLE POINT (reuse sampleEraserStroke, eraserHitTest.js:69-86) the single topmost erase-permitted hit = the candidate with the highest objects[] index (index order is proven z-order via SVGAnnotationLayer.jsx:2045), treating an imported-PDF appearance composite (getPdfAppearanceCompositeId, pageSpaceEraser.js:1126) as one unit ranked by its highest member index; the final delete set is the union of per-sample topmost winners. Per-sample (not per-gesture) resolution keeps a long drag able to delete the top object of each separate stack it crosses while never penetrating any single stack. Resolve topmost AMONG permitted candidates (after canErase/getEraseBlockReason) so a locked or foreign-owned top object doesn't invisibly shield an erasable one. Cross-lane ordering: survey markers and callouts render in dedicated layers above objects[], so in entire mode a marker/callout hit at a sample point outranks any objects[] hit at that point. Everything downstream is untouched: the narrowed objectMutations/targets flow through buildEraseIntent → prepareEraseIntentForCommit → commitDurableEraseIntent and the per-target undo restore actions (annotationEraseCommitPlan.js:307) unchanged. EDGE CASES the implementation must handle: (a) partial vs full — multiple overlapping ink strokes still all carve in partial mode (industry standard; only non-ink becomes untouchable); (b) undo/redo — history is already per-target so fewer targets just restore fewer objects, but the PDFViewer source-assertion tests and load-sensitive perf tests (partialEraserComplexity) assert current behavior and will need updating; (c) zoom mid-erase — zoomGeneration auto-commits the in-progress gesture at zoom-start; the topmost resolution uses page-unit points that are zoom-invariant, so the committed prefix and post-zoom continuation stay consistent; do NOT touch the signal; (d) collab echo — another user's objects already fail canModify (FabricEraserCanvas.jsx:1526-1530) and are re-validated server-side of the transaction (PDFViewer.jsx:27100-27115); topmost resolution must run after that filter, and a concurrent remote insert changing indices between preview and commit is safe because commit re-runs selection against annotationsRef at pointer-up; (e) imported PDF annotations — imported /Ink stays partial-eligible (eraserPolicy.js pdfAnnotationType check); imported non-ink stays annotation-atomic and its multi-layer appearance group must be ranked and deleted as one unit (pageSpaceEraser.js:1153-1168); (f) mode plumbing — eraserMode default is 'partial' (FabricEraserCanvas.jsx:270), so Part 1 alone fixes the reported complaint for the default tool; verify the toolbar's entire-mode UX copy still promises whole-object delete before shipping Part 2.

rootCause: Z-order is modeled ONLY as transient array position in React state; the durable Yjs store cannot represent it, and a cloud self-echo clobbers it on the next real edit. Details: (1) Stacking = position in `page.objects`; the SVG layer paints objects in array order (later index = on top) with no z field anywhere — docs/ANNOTATION-CONTRACT.md has no ordering contract. (2) Bring to Front/Forward/Backward/Back (`handleReorderAnnotation`, and the multi-select `reorderAll`) splice-and-reinsert the local array and save it — this correctly updates React state, so it LOOKS like it worked. (3) But persistence goes through `syncByPageToDoc`, which diffs a keyed Y.Map (`annotations`: storageKey -> {p, o}) per-object: a pure permutation changes no object payload, so `shallowEntryEqual` is true for every entry and ZERO Yjs ops are written. The reorder never reaches the durable store. (4) The read side, `docToByPage`, materializes each page's array in Y.Map key-insertion order (explicitly documented in the code) — i.e., original creation order. (5) When the user then MOVES any object, that move DOES produce a Yjs op, which is appended to Supabase `annotation_updates`. The realtime INSERT subscription deliberately applies self-authored rows too ("Apply matching rows too... True self-echoes are Yjs no-ops") and unconditionally calls `notifyChange`, which rebuilds ALL pages via `docToByPage` (insertion order) and pushes that into `setAnnotationsByPage` via the `handle.onChange` listener — replacing the locally reordered array with the original-order array. A drops back behind B. The hook's "local edits do NOT echo back from the store" comment is true only for the direct doc-update observer; the cloud round-trip echo path violates it. Note the bug is two-layer: even with the echo suppressed, the reorder would still silently vanish on reload, because it was never persisted at all (and Y.Map insertion order is not even guaranteed identical across clients, so it was never a valid ordering source).

professionalBehavior: A z-order change is a durable document mutation, exactly like moving or recoloring a shape (Figma/Illustrator/Bluebeam semantics): once the user brings A above B, that stacking must survive every subsequent edit by any user, survive save/reload, replicate to collaborators, and participate in undo/redo as one step. It must never depend on a CRDT map's key-insertion order, which is both unwritable (a permutation diffs to zero ops) and not guaranteed consistent across clients.
proposedFix: Persist an explicit per-annotation fractional order key and honor it on materialization. (1) Write: stamp `obj.data.zOrder` (fractional-index string, LexoRank-style, to avoid float-gap exhaustion; tiebreak by annotation id for cross-client determinism) inside handleReorderAnnotation (PDFViewer.jsx:25875) and reorderAll (useAnnotationContextMenu.jsx:501) — compute a key between the new neighbors so ONLY the moved object(s) change payload. Because the field rides in the object JSON, it flows through the existing contract unchanged: handleSaveAnnotations -> capture effect -> syncByPageToDoc now sees a real payload diff and emits a normal per-object Yjs op. (2) Read: in docToByPage (annotationDocStore.js:682), as the FINAL step (after eraser-lane rebase, which looks objects up by storageKey/index and should keep operating on insertion-order arrays), stable-sort each page's objects by (zOrder ?? sentinel-keeping-insertion-order, then id). SVG render and hit-testing keep using array order — no other component changes. Edge cases: UNDO/REDO — zOrder lives in the object payload, so buildAnnotationHistoryAction diffs capture and restore it automatically; verify normalizeCanvasJsonForHistory does not strip unknown data fields. CONCURRENT REORDERS — per-object Y.Map LWW: different objects merge cleanly; same object converges to one writer; identical keys break ties by id so all clients agree. SAVE/RELOAD — the sort makes order durable, also fixing the currently-latent reload loss. COPY/PASTE/DUPLICATE — clear or re-mint zOrder on the clone so pasted objects land on top rather than interleaving at the source's depth. IMPORTED PDF ANNOTATIONS — leave zOrder unset on import (sentinel preserves import order, avoids rewriting thousands of entries and keeps re-import idempotent); stamp only on user reorder. COUNTERS — deriveCounterPresentationNumbers orders by createdAt, unaffected. SELECTION FOLLOW — pendingSvgSelection indices must be computed against the post-sort array (they already are once local state and doc materialization sort identically). Separately, consider making the realtime echo notifyChange skip when applyAuthoritativeCloudRow was a pure self-echo no-op (annotationDocSync.js:2916-2926) — a hygiene win that stops local state being replaced by doc materializations gratuitously — but the persisted key is the real fix; suppressing the echo alone would only hide the loss until reload.
